questions.question: Let A = {a, b, c}. What is the equivalence relation of smallest cardinality on A? What is the equivalence relation of largest cardinality on A?
steps: An equivalence relation must be reflexive, symmetric and transitive.
These three pairs alone are symmetric and transitive, so the smallest relation has 3 pairs.
Every relation on A is a subset of A × A.
A × A contains all nine ordered pairs and is itself reflexive, symmetric and transitive.
Thus the largest equivalence relation is A × A, containing 9 pairs.

questions.question: In the set Z of integers, define mRn if m − n is divisible by 7. Prove that R is an equivalence relation.
steps: Reflexive: m − m = 0 = 7 × 0, so mRm for every integer m.
Symmetric: if m − n = 7k, then n − m = 7(−k), so nRm.
Transitive: if m − n = 7k and n − p = 7j, then m − p = 7(k+j), so mRp.
Therefore R is reflexive, symmetric and transitive, hence an equivalence relation.
